Estimate the equation of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round both the slope and the $y$-intercept to the nearest $0.5.$
worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/fdad2c939372e14617ba4e393037d7f5852cd8114467aa914ccb8963c0eacfeb.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(2,5)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(6,1).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-5}{6-2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{4} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-1$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-x+b \\ 5 & =-2+b \\ 7 & =b \\ b & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-x+7.
$$
